members.name: MLCActivationTypeNone
members.doc: The identity activation type.

members.name: MLCActivationTypeReLU
members.doc: The ReLU activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = x >= 0 ? x : a * x \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeLinear
members.doc: The linear activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = a * x + b \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeSigmoid
members.doc: The sigmoid activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = 1 / (1 + e⁻ˣ) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeHardSigmoid
members.doc: The hard sigmoid activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = clamp((x * a) + b, 0, 1) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeTanh
members.doc: The hyperbolic tangent (TanH) activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = a * tanh(b * x) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeAbsolute
members.doc: The absolute activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = fabs(x) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeSoftPlus
members.doc: The parametric soft plus activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = a * log(1 + e^(b * x)) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeSoftSign
members.doc: The parametric soft sign activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = x / (1 + abs(x)) \endcod

members.name: MLCActivationTypeELU
members.doc: The parametric ELU activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = x >= 0 ? x : a * (exp(x) - 1) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeReLUN
members.doc: The ReLUN activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = min((x >= 0 ? x : a * x), b) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeLogSigmoid
members.doc: The log sigmoid activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = log(1 / (1 + exp(-x))) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeSELU
members.doc: The SELU activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = scale * (max(0, x) + min(0, α * (exp(x) − 1))) \endcode where: \code α = 1.6732632423543772848170429916717 scale = 1.0507009873554804934193349852946 \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeCELU
members.doc: The CELU activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = max(0, x) + min(0, a * (exp(x / a) − 1)) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeHardShrink
members.doc: The hard shrink activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = x, if x > a or x < −a, else 0 \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeSoftShrink
members.doc: The soft shrink activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = x - a, if x > a, x + a, if x < −a, else 0 \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeTanhShrink
members.doc: The hyperbolic tangent (TanH) shrink activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = x - tanh(x) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeThreshold
members.doc: The threshold activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = x, if x > a, else b \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeGELU
members.doc: The GELU activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = x * CDF(x) \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeHardSwish
members.doc: The hardswish activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = 0, if x <= -3 f(x) = x, if x >= +3 f(x) = x * (x + 3)/6, otherwise \endcode

members.name: MLCActivationTypeClamp
members.doc: The clamp activation type. @discussion This activation type implements the following function: \code f(x) = min(max(x, a), b) \endcode

members.name: MLCDeviceTypeANE
members.doc: The  Apple Neural Engine device.  When selected, the framework will use the  Neural Engine to execute all layers that can be executed on it. Layers that cannot be executed on the ANE will run on the CPU or GPU.   The Neural Engine device must be explicitly selected.  MLDeviceTypeAny will not select the Neural Engine device.  In addition, this device can be used with inference graphs only.  This device cannot be used with a training graph or an inference graph that shares layers with a training graph.

members.name: MLCExecutionOptionsSkipWritingInputDataToDevice
members.doc: The option to skip writing input data to device memory. @discussion this option to prevent writing the input tensors to device memory associated with these tensors when the framework executes the graph.

members.name: MLCExecutionOptionsSynchronous
members.doc: The option to execute the graph synchronously. @discussion Include this option to wait until execution of the graph on specified device finishes before returning from the \p execute method.

members.name: MLCExecutionOptionsProfiling
members.doc: The option to return profiling information in the callback before returning from execution. @discussion Include this option to return profliling information in the graph execute completion handler callback, including device execution time.

members.name: MLCExecutionOptionsForwardForInference
members.doc: The option to execute the forward pass for inference only. @discussion If you include this option and execute a training graph using one of the \p execute methods, such as \p -executeWithInputsData:lossLabelsData:lossLabelWeightsData:batchSize:options:completionHandler: , the framework only executes the forward pass of the training graph, and it executes that forward pass for inference only. If you include this option and execute a training graph using one of the executeForward methods, such as \p -executeForwardWithBatchSize:options:completionHandler:), the framework executes the forward pass for inference only.

members.name: MLCExecutionOptionsPerLayerProfiling
members.doc: The option to enable additional per layer profiling information currently emitted using signposts. @discussion The option to enable per layer profiling information emitted as signposts. The per layer information can be visualized using the Logging Instrument in Xcode's Instruments. This information may not be available for all MLCDevice.

members.name: MLCGraphCompilationOptionsDebugLayers
members.doc: The option to debug layers during graph compilation. @discussion Include this option to disable various optimizations such as layer fusion, and ensure the framework synchronizes the resulting forward and gradients tensors host memory with device memory, for layers marked as debuggable.

members.name: MLCGraphCompilationOptionsDisableLayerFusion
members.doc: The option to disable layer fusion during graph compilation. @discussion Include this option to disable fusion of layers, which is an important optimization that helps performance and memory footprint.

members.name: MLCGraphCompilationOptionsLinkGraphs
members.doc: The option to link graphs during graph compilation. @discussion Include this option when you link together one or more sub-graphs when executing the forward, gradient, and optimizer update. For example, if the full computation graph includes a layer that the framework doesn’t support, you’ll need to create multiple sub-graphs and link them together using \p MLCGraphCompilationOptionsLinkGraphs. When doing so, include this option when you call \p -compileWithOptions: for graphs you want to link together.

members.name: MLCGraphCompilationOptionsComputeAllGradients
members.doc: The option to compute all gradients during graph compilation. @discussion Include this option to compute gradients for layers with or without parameters that only take input tensors. For example, if the first layer of a graph is a convolution layer, the framework only computes the gradients for weights and biases associated with the convolution layer, but not the gradients for the input. Include this option if you want to compute all gradients for the input.
